extracted.intended_audience: educated general readers and naturalists (students of biology)
extracted.subtask_description: Explain and evaluate how the surrounding medium (environmental agencies/forces) directly initiates differentiation between outer and inner parts of organisms, and how those physical initiations interact with inherited tendencies and natural selection. Uses embryology, plant and animal examples, and inorganic analogies as evidential criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary differentiation ascribed to direct action of the medium
rubrics_metrics.description: If every portion of a protoplasmic body, when isolated, immediately surrounds itself with a skin that arises at the surface of contact with sap or water, then this primary differentiation of outer from inner must be ascribed to the direct action of the medium.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples cited: spores, pollen, fragments of Vaucheria protoplasm that round into globular bodies with a hyaline envelope denser than the inner substance (pp. 10, 13-14, 41-42). The text emphasizes that the site of initiation (surface contact) is key evidence for medium causation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Whether coating is secreted or transformed is immaterial to causal attribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the coating around protoplasm is secreted by the protoplasm or results from transformation of it matters not to the argument: in either case the action of the medium causes its formation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The distinction between secretion vs transformation does not overturn the conclusion that the medium initiates the outer layer; natural selection then acts on resulting variations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Physical initiation provides raw material for natural selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Many varied and complex differentiations which developed cell-walls display must be considered as originating from variations of this physically-generated covering, which natural selection has taken advantage of.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The author frames natural selection as acting on variations that are often initiated by environmental (physico-chemical) effects rather than being solely spontaneously generated and then selected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Persistent externality leads to specialized outer coating
rubrics_metrics.description: When a certain part of the substance remains permanently external in position, it is followed by transformation of it into a coating unlike the substance it contains.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Illustrated by transitions from imprisoned amoeba-like protoplasm to free amoebae, and by Foraminifera which, though internally simple, secrete calcareous shells determined by inherited constitution but initiated by contact with the medium.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analogy with inorganic bodies: expect an active surface between changed outer layer and unchanged inner mass
rubrics_metrics.description: In inorganic masses modifiable by their medium, between an outer changed layer and an inner unchanged mass there is a surface where active change is going on; a similar relation suggests medium-driven change in cells and organisms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as an inferential standard: comparable distributions of changed outer layer / active surface / inner mass in inorganic and organic cases support medium causation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exposure-to-environment correlates with degree of epidermal differentiation
rubrics_metrics.description: The contrast between outer (epidermal) and inner tissue is the plainer the more the part of the plant (or organ) concerned is exposed to air and light: outermost layers consist of smaller, firmer cells; inner cells are larger and sometimes long.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cites Sachs and general botanical observations: leaves, algal layers, and epidermal cuticle as evidence that exposure drives structural differentiation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unexposed vs exposed roots demonstrate medium effect
rubrics_metrics.description: Imbedded (unexposed) roots have comparatively thin outer protective coats, whereas roots permanently exposed to light and air acquire coverings allied to branch coverings, showing direct environmental causation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to rebut the claim that such differences are wholly due to natural selection of favourable variations; exposure provides immediate causative explanation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mechanical forces (pressure/friction) produce predictable tissue changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Continuous pressure on a surface causes absorption, intermittent pressure causes growth; friction and intermittent pressure produce ribbed skin on hands and feet where usage is greatest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: corns and blisters (superficial tissues changed unrelated to adaptive needs), sailors' hands strongly ribbed, unused hands becoming smooth. These are cited as mechanically produced and non-adaptive changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regeneration/healing shows medium-driven formation of protective coverings
rubrics_metrics.description: When deep layers that normally do not produce outward growth are called on (e.g., in wide ulcers or burns), a new outward-growing 'pro-skin' is produced that lacks hair-follicles and other specialities of the original skin but functions as a protective covering.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This phenomenon indicates the role of immediate medium influence in initiating protective layers rather than a full hereditary recreation of species-typical structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exposure can override inherited proclivity producing divergence from type
rubrics_metrics.description: When mucous membrane is exposed to air (e.g., by eversion/protrusion), it can assume the general character and microscopic structure of ordinary skin (cylinders shorten to flat cells producing squamous epithelium), a divergence from the species' normal type.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The change occurs in a short time and shows the medium's effect may overcome inherited tendencies rather than merely complete a preexisting type.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spatial distribution of living/modified tissue: cambium produces outer bark and inner wood
rubrics_metrics.description: In exogenous stems the cambium layer (a place of predominant vital activity) grows inwards forming wood and outwards forming bark, producing an outer covering changed by the medium and an inner film of highest vitality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This botanical tissue-distribution is used as a general model for how environmental effects produce outer changed layers while inner tissues remain highly living and sheltered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embryonic layer contact predicts adult role: epiblast/hypoblast/mesoblast criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: Out of the outer embryonic layer (epiblast) arise epidermis, nervous system, and sense organs (structures interfacing with the medium); out of the introverted layer (hypoblast) arise the alimentary canal and associated secretory parts; out of the mesoblast arise bones, muscles, heart and blood-vessels — structures that never had direct intercourse with the environment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This embryological origin-to-function mapping is presented as strong evidence that contact with the environment in early development pre-determines later external/interfacing structures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Origin of central nervous system from epidermis as evidence of function concentration
rubrics_metrics.description: The central nervous system and ganglion-cells are originally derived from the undifferentiated epithelial cells of the surface; functions once taken by the whole skin became concentrated in a special part of the skin which was step by step removed from the surface.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quoted from Balfour: embryological evidence that sensory and nervous functions evolved by invagination and concentration of epidermal tissue, supporting the general thesis about environmental interface driving structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invagination plausibly primitive for forming two-layered gastrula
rubrics_metrics.description: The double covering stage (gastrula) can be reached by invagination or delamination; on a priori grounds invagination is favored as the original way, exemplified in lowest types and illustrated by the india-rubber ball cup analogy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This developmental-mechanism criterion underpins the argument about which parts of the embryo remain in contact with the medium (epiblast) vs. which are introverted (hypoblast) and later give rise to external vs internal structures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Empirical observation of protoplasmic fragments forming denser envelopes supports medium causation
rubrics_metrics.description: Masses of protoplasm escaping into water from injured sacs often instantly become rounded into globular bodies with a hyaline protoplasm envelope denser than the inner watery substance — evidence that the medium induces a skin.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This specific empirical fact is used as a concrete test: if isolated living matter exposed to medium develops an envelope, then the medium is a causal agent in outer-layer formation.
